hero.subtitle: A fall on someone else's property can leave you with medical bills and a lot of questions about what happens next. LawProactive connects Coronado residents and visitors with an independent attorney who handles premises liability claims on the island and across San Diego County.

about.title: Coronado Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Coronado draws heavy foot traffic between its beaches, hotels, and shops along Orange Avenue and 3rd and 4th Streets, and that mix of visitors and locals means property conditions matter. A wet lobby floor, a cracked sidewalk near a storefront, uneven pavers at a beachfront property, or poor lighting in a parking structure can all lead to a fall that causes real injury. California law asks whether the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn people about it. That's why documenting the scene matters so much: photos of the hazard, the names of any witnesses, and a request that surveillance footage be preserved before it's overwritten. LawProactive doesn't handle claims directly - we connect people who've been hurt on someone else's property with an independent attorney who can evaluate the notice question, gather evidence, and explain what a claim might look like given your specific situation. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to move forward.

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises liability claims turn on whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help figure out what evidence supports that before it disappears.

items.title: Preserving Video Matters Early
items.desc: Businesses often overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference in a premises claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California is a pure comparative fault state, so even if you're partly responsible for a fall, you may still be able to recover a portion of your damages.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Coronado?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government entity, like the City of Coronado, might be responsible for the hazard, the deadline is much shorter and involves an early claim filing requirement. It's worth talking to an attorney as soon as possible to sort out which timeline applies.

items.question: What should I do right after falling at a Coronado hotel or business?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of exactly what caused the fall, note the time, and ask that any surveillance video be preserved. Coronado's hotels, restaurants, and beachfront properties often have cameras covering entryways and walkways, so a prompt written request can help make sure that footage isn't deleted before an attorney can review it.

items.question: Can I still recover damages if I was partly at fault for the fall?
items.answer: Yes. California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated entirely. An independent attorney can help evaluate how the facts of your fall might be viewed under this standard.
